written_by: hand, from the designs' meaning and an independent simulation oracle (oracle/); never from eqy output

designs.alu.v: gold: a registered 8-bit ALU, y <= r and z <= (r == 0), r = a+b, a-b, a&b or a^b by op
designs.gate.v: a gate-level netlist of alu.v (synth -flatten; abc -g AND,OR,XOR,MUX). It keeps an internal wire named r
designs.gate_bad.v: gate.v with one AND gate flipped to OR (line 147)

oracle.what: oracle/tb.v clocks every (op, a, b) vector, all 2^18 of them plus the reset vector, through a design with Icarus Verilog and prints y and z; oracle/compare.py diffs two such dumps
oracle.gate.v: equal to alu.v on every vector
oracle.gate_bad.v: differs from alu.v in y on some vectors and in z on some vectors, under every op

alu_pass.why: A false FAIL. gate.v is equivalent to alu.v (oracle), but with the default configuration eqy matches the gold r against the gate wire also named r and cuts the designs there. Gold computes z from r (z <= r == 0). ABC restructured the gate side: z's next value is _038_ & _055_ (gate.v line 184), internal nodes of the r logic, not r itself. So the gold z partition starts at the cut r while the gate z partition reaches back to the primary inputs, and with r free the two cannot be proved equal. The y partition is a plain register on r on both sides (gate.v lines 282 to 305) and proves; the r partition is the whole ALU on both sides and proves. The failure is in the configuration, not the design.

alu_pass2.why: The same correct netlist with [match alu] gold-nomatch r, so r is no longer a match point and the partitions run from the inputs to the registered outputs y and z. Equivalent by the oracle, so every partition proves.

alu_fail.why: The mutant differs from the gold in both y and z (oracle). Whatever the partitioning, a real difference cannot prove. With the default cut at r, the flipped gate sits inside the r partition, so r fails; z fails for the alu_pass reason and the mutation; y is a plain register on the cut r on both sides and proves.

alu_fail2.why: With gold-nomatch r the partitions are the registered outputs. The flipped gate lies in the cone of r, which feeds both y and z, and the oracle shows both differ, so the partition for y and the partition for z both fail.
